Vṛṣṭinemi and Sudharmā; Riṣṭanemi and Suvarcā, as well as Śaryāti; Sudharmā and Mṛdu; Subhūmi and Bahubhūmi; and the two women Śraviṣṭhā and Śravaṇā. || 12 ||
From Andhaka, the daughter of Kaśya gave birth to four sons:
Kukura, Bhajamāna, Śami, and Kambalabarhiṣa. || 13 ||
The son of Kukura was Vṛṣṇi; the son of Vṛṣṇi was Dhṛti;
his son was Kapotaroman, and Tittiri was his son. || 14 ||
Her son was the learned Nala, the friend of Tumburu;
indeed, he is renowned by the name Candanodakadundubhi. || 15 ||
Abhijit was his son, and from him Punarvasu was born.
Previously childless, Abhijit, that best of men, being urged by the sages, joyfully performed a horse sacrifice for the sake of obtaining a son. || 16 ||
From the midst of that *atirātra* sacrifice, he rose up from the center of the assembly;
therefore, he was wise, a knower of dharma, a performer of sacrifices, a donor, and possessed of great wealth. || 17 ||
To him was born a pair of children, it is said, from Abhijit:
Āhuka and Āhukī, both renowned as the best among the wise. || 18 ||
And regarding this, they cite these verses concerning that Āhuka:
"Of those [chariots] equipped with quivers and undercarriages, adorned with banners and protective fenders... (19)
There were indeed ten thousand chariots with a roar like thunderclouds;
yet there was no one there who spoke untruth, none who lacked splendor, none who had not performed sacrifices, and none who had not given in thousands.
For he was neither impure nor ignorant,
as he was born among those who partake of food;
he obtained the maintenance of Āhuka.
This, indeed, is what is being said. || 21 ||
Neither the impure, nor the ignorant,
nor anyone other than a Bhoja became superior;
they reached as far as Āhuka.
Thus, this is called the positive concomitance (anvaya). || 21 ||
Āhuka also gave his sister Āhukī to the king of the Avantis;
and from Āhuka, the daughter of the King of Kāśī gave birth to two sons.
Both Devaka and Ugrasena were equal to the offspring of gods;
from Devaka were born heroic sons who resembled the thirty deities. || 23 ||
Devavān, Upadeva, Sudeva, and Devarakṣita—they had seven sisters, whom he gave to Vasudeva: || 24 ||
Devakī, Śrutadevī, Mitradevī, Yaśodharā,
Śrīdevī, and Satyadevī.
And "sutāpī" is the seventh [case]. || 25 ||
Devakī, Śrutadevā, Yaśodā, Śrutiśravā,
Śrīdevā, and Upadevā.
And "surūpā" is the seventh [case]. || 25 ||
To one who has no son, two sons of equal vigor are born;
those who have no sons are truly valiant.
There were three of supreme renown:
Sudamṣṭra, Sunābha, and Kṛṣṇa; these are considered the Andhakas. || 36 ||
The man who constantly recites this lineage of the Andhakas attains for himself a vast lineage and becomes possessed of progeny. || 37 ||
The daughter of Ikṣvāku gave birth to a heroic son, Devamīdhuṣa.
From Mīdhuṣa and Śūra were born ten sons through Bhojā.
The mighty-armed Vasudeva was born first, followed by Ānakadundubhi;
then Devabhāga was born, and after him, Devaśravas. || 39 ||
Anādhṛṣṭi, Śini, and Nanda along with the Sṛñjayas;
Śyāma, Śamīka, and Saṃyūpa; and five excellent women of the Aśva lineage. || 40 ||
Śrutakīrti, Pṛthā, Śrutadevī, Śrutaśravā, and Rājādhidevī—these five were the mothers of heroes. || 41 ||
Śrutadevī bore a son to Kṛta, who was named Sugrīva. Then, when he had grown up, he gave Pṛthā to Kuntibhoja out of friendship.
Thus was Pṛthā, the sister of Vasudeva, known as Kuntī. || 44 ||
That blameless woman was given by Vasudeva as the wife of Pāṇḍu;
through Pāṇḍu she gave birth to sons of gods who were great chariot-warriors. || 45 ||
From Dharma was born Yudhiṣṭhira; from Vāta was born Vṛkodara; and from Indra was born Dhanañjaya, whose prowess is equal to that of Śakra. || 46 ||
He who was born from three persons, a great chariot-warrior by virtue of his three portions, the performer of the gods' work and the slayer of all the Dānavas. || 461 ||
He by whom the Dānavas, who were incapable of being slain even by Śakra, were destroyed;
he, having regained his splendor, was established in the triple heaven by Śakra.
We have heard that Nakula and Sahadeva were born of Mādravatī, endowed with beauty, strength, and all virtuous qualities. || 47 ||
Rohiṇī, named Pauravī, was the wife of Ānakadundubhi;
she bore as her eldest son Rāma, as well as Sāraṇa who is fond of battle, Durdama, Damana, Subhrū, Piṇḍāraka, and Mahāhanu. || 48 ||
Then two daughters with beautiful eyes were born to Rohiṇī;
and to Devakī, the wife of Śūra, Suṣeṇa and Kīrtimān were also born.
Udāsī, Bhadrasena, and likewise Rṣivāsa, with Bhadravideha as the sixth—Kaṃsa caused all of them to be slain. || 482 ||
On that first new moon which will occur in the rainy season,
the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, the progenitor of beings, was formerly born. || 49 ||
Subhadrā, the sweet-spoken one, was born after Kṛṣṇā. || 50 ||
The highly effulgent and illustrious Śūra was born of Devakī;
Sahadeva, the upholder of the lineage, was born of Tāmrā as a descendant of Śūra. || 50 ||
Devarakṣitā obtained a son who carried a sword in its sheath, and a single fortunate daughter; Kaṃsa killed her as well. || 50 ||
Vijaya, Rocamāna, Vardhamāna, and Devala—
all these great-souled ones were born of Upadevī.
The high-souled Agāvaha was begotten by Vṛkadevī.
He was born of Vṛkadevī himself, known by the name Mandaka. 52.
Devakī bore as her seventh son Madana, a highly fortunate seeker who was unconquered in battles. || 53 ||
Formerly, while wandering in the forest at the monastery of Śrīdādevī, Śauri begot an eldest son, Kauśika, upon a Vaiśya woman. || 54 ||
Sutanu and Vanaraji were the two wives of Śauri;
and Puṇḍra and Kapila were the two powerful sons of Vasudeva. || 55 ||
There was a Niṣāda named Jarā who was among the foremost of archers;
both Saubhadra and Bhava were also of great being. || 56 ||
The son of Devabhāga was also known by the name Uddhava; they call the most excellent Devaśravas the foremost among the learned. || 57 ||
The illustrious Aikṣvākī obtained offspring from Anādhṛṣṭi:
Śatrughna, who put an end to his enemies; from him was born Śrāddha. || 58 ||
Kṛṣṇa, being pleased with Gaṇḍūṣa who was childless, granted him a son—Sucandra, who was highly fortunate, heroic, and possessed of great strength. || 59 ||
These two sons of Jāmbavatī, Cārudeṣṇa and Sāmba, possess auspicious marks and are heroic and exceedingly strong. || 59 ||
Both Rantipāla and Ranti were the two sons of Nandana;
and the four sons of Śamīka were valiant and possessed of great strength. || 60 ||
Viraja, Dhanu, Śyāma, and likewise Śṛñjaya—Śyāma was childless, while Śamīka went to the forest;
loathing the status of a Bhoja, he attained the rank of a royal sage (rājarṣi). || 61 ||
The man who constantly glorifies the birth and exaltation of Kṛṣṇa, or who constantly hears it, is liberated from all sins. || 62 ||
